children: first foldable iPhone is earning praise for its refined design and practical features ahead of its Friday, Oct. 23, release, with reviewers describing the device as a polished entry into a market pioneered by Samsung (SSNLF), according to reviews published.

Duo opens from a compact handset into a 7.6-inch display, giving users more room for multitasking, messaging and email. Reviewers highlighted its sturdy hinge, comfortable folded design and nanotexture display, which helps make the screen crease less noticeable. The early reception suggests Apple may have found a compelling way to bring its familiar user experience to foldable phones.

Chance Miller of 9to5Mac praised the device's engineering, while WIRED's Julian Chokkattu described Apple's first attempt as more refined than earlier generations of competing foldables. The phone also carries an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance, adding protection to its flexible design.

The roughly $2,000 price and limited app optimization remain considerations, while Touch ID replaces Face ID. Still, strong preorder demand has pushed some delivery estimates to late January, even before broad market availability begins Friday. Apple's entry could expand its presence in premium smartphones and give the company a fresh opportunity to compete with Samsung in foldables.

title: Good News For Apple Stock Fans
